headline: Record gold prices lift profit despite lower output
summary_short: Sales rose 15% y/y to $6.4B on a $4,317/oz realized gold price; net income was $2.5B and free cash flow $1.9B despite 8.5% lower gold output and AISC of $1,454/oz.
summary_long: Newmont produced 1.3Moz of attributable gold plus 11Moz of silver and 23kt of copper, and remains on track for 5.3Moz in 2026. By-product CAS was $832/oz and AISC $1,454/oz; full-year cost guidance improved to $925/oz and $1,520/oz. The company ended with $8.8B of cash and a $3.2B net cash position before a planned $1.95B payment to Barrick under the amended Nevada Gold Mines agreement. A $0.26 dividend was declared.
confidence_notes: AISC, CAS (by-product) are net of by-product credits; co-product AISC was $1,963/oz and is not comparable. Adjusted net income and free cash flow are non-GAAP. Y/y comparisons use the Q3 2025 column in the release's summary table. Production is attributable.

drivers.explanation: Average realized gold price of $4,317 per ounce versus $3,539 a year ago more than offset lower production.
Release does not give a detailed cause for the year-over-year cost increase; full-year cost guidance was improved.
CEO says the company is on track for full-year production guidance and an improved cost outlook, with disciplined operational execution.
